bug_description.normalized: In the exact staged vulnerable MapServer checkout `ae65a28202c50fc134b98b3137e1735665a270e1`, the 157-byte witness is parsed as a `.map` file that enters `MAP -> SCALEBAR` and routes label content into the embedded `scalebar->label`. The visible bytes and the saved allocation stack show that parsing reaches `STYLE` for that embedded label and `msGrowLabelStyles()` allocates the label's `styles` array. The later crash in `freeLabel()` proves that at least one execution of `label->numstyles++;` completed on that same object, so `label->numstyles` became nonzero, although the saved artifacts do not pin the exact count. The saved free stack separately shows that a `loadLabel(&(scalebar->label))` invocation reaches `EOF` at `mapfile.c:1620` and executes `freeLabel(label)` on that same owner-managed embedded object; the artifacts do not distinguish whether this is the same `loadLabel()` invocation that published the styles or a later re-entry from `loadScalebar()`. That `freeLabel()` call frees the heap-allocated `label->styles` array at `mapfile.c:1512` but does not null `label->styles` or reset `label->numstyles`. `loadMapInternal()` propagates the parse failure back to `msLoadMap()`, which tears down the whole map and revisits the same embedded label through `msFreeMap() -> freeScalebar() -> freeLabel()`. On that second cleanup traversal, `freeLabel()` uses the stale nonzero `numstyles` and dereferences `label->styles[0]` from the freed array, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` at `mapfile.c:1506`. The fix commit removes the `freeLabel(label)` call from the `EOF` case so only the owning map cleanup frees the embedded label.

source.description: First project parser statement that creates the vulnerability-relevant ownership state. Once the witness token stream reaches `LABEL` inside `SCALEBAR`, `loadScalebar()` parses directly into the embedded `scalebar->label` field, so later allocations and frees operate on an owner-managed object that `msFreeMap()` will revisit on error cleanup.
source.value_from: The saved witness `gt_results/arvo_52102/poc` is exactly 157 bytes (sha256 `47da868794954caef5c36dc0184ca46e52bbe16b85d39529670cf739c87ee932`). Its visible ASCII bytes begin with `MAP` and `SCALEBAR`, later contain `LABEL` and `STYLE` tokens plus embedded NUL/non-printable bytes, and the file ends without enough `END` tokens to close the nested `SCALEBAR`/`LABEL` parsing cleanly. Those bytes make `loadMapInternal()` dispatch into `loadScalebar()` and parse label content into the embedded `scalebar->label` object.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. During the second cleanup traversal of the embedded scalebar label, `freeLabel()` enters the style loop with `i == 0` and dereferences `label->styles[0]` through the already-freed `label->styles` array.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free ... READ of size 8` at `freeLabel /src/MapServer/mapfile.c:1506:8`, with `freeScalebar`, `msFreeMap`, and `msLoadMap` immediately below it in the crash stack.

root_cause.code: freeLabel(label);       /* free any structures allocated before EOF */
root_cause.description: Premature invalidation of an owner-managed object. When `loadLabel()` hits `EOF`, it frees the embedded `scalebar->label` in place even though ownership still belongs to the partially built `mapObj`, so the later map teardown walks the same label again.
root_cause.note: The patch removes this exact statement from the `EOF` arm, expressing the missing ownership obligation: `loadLabel()` must not free `scalebar->label` here because `msFreeMap()` is still responsible for that embedded object.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first concrete lifetime-relevant heap object. A `STYLE` token on the embedded `scalebar->label` makes `msGrowLabelStyles()` allocate the `label->styles` pointer array; ASan's allocation stack points to this exact `realloc`.

parser_admitted.description: The witness is admitted as a `SCALEBAR` block inside the map parser, so control enters `loadScalebar()` on the live `map->scalebar` object and the vulnerable embedded-label path becomes reachable.

evidence_limitations: The staged vulnerable workspace checkout `ae65a28202c50fc134b98b3137e1735665a270e1` differs from the metadata field `vulnerable_commit`. This GT is grounded in the staged checkout because its source lines match the saved sanitizer trace and staged patch context.

The witness contains embedded NUL and other non-printable bytes between the visible keywords. Stage 02 therefore claims only the facts forced by the saved PoC bytes, the ASan stacks, and the source semantics: parsing of `scalebar->label` reaches at least one successful `STYLE` publication so `label->numstyles > 0`, and a `loadLabel(&(scalebar->label))` invocation reaches `EOF` and frees that same embedded object. The saved artifacts do not fix the exact style count or whether the `EOF`-arm free happens in the same `loadLabel()` invocation that published the style count.

fine_trace.note: Source. When the witness token stream reaches `LABEL` inside `SCALEBAR`, parsing is redirected into the embedded `scalebar->label` field. That alias means any cleanup done inside `loadLabel()` acts on the same owner-managed object that `msFreeMap()` later owns and frees.

On a `STYLE` token for that embedded label, `msGrowLabelStyles()` allocates the `styleObj *` array later freed and re-read. `initLabel()` had started this label with `numstyles = maxstyles = 0` and `styles = NULL`, and ASan's allocation stack is anchored at this line.

At least one `STYLE` sub-parse on the embedded label completes successfully and executes this increment, making `label->numstyles` nonzero from its init value 0. The later sink proves the second `freeLabel()` loop enters with `i = 0`, but the saved artifacts do not establish the exact final count.

fine_trace.code: freeLabel(label);       /* free any structures allocated before EOF */
fine_trace.note: Root cause. A `loadLabel(&(scalebar->label))` invocation on this embedded label object reaches `EOF`, so the `EOF` arm frees the owner-managed `label` in place instead of leaving cleanup to the enclosing map owner. The saved stacks tie this free to the `loadScalebar()` callsite, but they do not distinguish whether it is the same or a later `loadLabel()` invocation than the one that made `label->numstyles` nonzero. The fix removes this exact call.

The `freeLabel()` reached from step 4 frees the styles array allocated in step 2. This function does not then set `label->styles = NULL` or reset `label->numstyles`, so the embedded label keeps a dangling array pointer and stale positive count after the `EOF` arm returns `-1`.

The parse error from step 4 propagates out of `loadMapInternal()`, so `msLoadMap()` immediately tears down the partially built `mapObj`. Because the freed label is embedded inside `map->scalebar`, this owner cleanup revisits the same object instead of discarding it silently.

During `msFreeMap()` teardown, the scalebar owner performs its normal cleanup and calls `freeLabel()` on the same embedded `scalebar->label` object that step 4 already freed internally. This is the stale-owner path to the sink.

Sink. In the second `freeLabel()` traversal, `label->numstyles` is still nonzero from step 3, so the loop enters with `i = 0` and reads `label->styles[0]` through the array pointer freed in step 5. ASan reports the resulting 8-byte heap-use-after-free read at this exact line.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, exact staged vulnerable source, and staged patch.diff; Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed revision

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_52102 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8` in `freeLabel` with stack `freeScalebar -> msFreeMap -> msLoadMap -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

format.name: Malformed MapServer .map file with embedded NUL bytes and unclosed SCALEBAR/LABEL content
format.contract: Exactly the 157-byte witness stored in `gt_results/arvo_52102/poc` (sha256 `47da868794954caef5c36dc0184ca46e52bbe16b85d39529670cf739c87ee932`). Its visible bytes begin with `MAP` and `SCALEBAR`, later contain multiple `LABEL`/`STYLE` tokens plus embedded NUL and other non-printable bytes, and end without enough `END` tokens to close the nested `SCALEBAR`/`LABEL` parsing cleanly. On the embedded `scalebar->label` object, that exact witness drives `msGrowLabelStyles()` allocation, reaches a state with `label->numstyles > 0`, and later makes a `loadLabel()` `EOF` arm call `freeLabel(label)` before the owner cleanup path `msLoadMap -> msFreeMap -> freeScalebar -> freeLabel` revisits the same object. The saved artifacts do not establish the exact style count or whether the `EOF` arm occurs in the same `loadLabel()` invocation that published the styles.
